legacy_cells.I: 048_2025_Distributed Learning for Heart Disease Risk Prediction Based on Key Clinical Parameters with Evaluation Metrics Analysis.pdf
legacy_cells.AI: Tabular clinical parameters: age; blood pressure; cholesterol; ECG findings; heart rate
legacy_cells.DN: UCI Heart Disease Dataset; Cleveland Clinic dataset
legacy_cells.FN: HDP-FLDec reports accuracy 94.2%, precision 92.8%, recall 93.6%, F1 93.2% and AUC-ROC 0.97 on UCI/Cleveland heart-disease benchmark data; reported accuracy gains over federated baselines were 5–7%. These are decentralized classification results, not longitudinal dynamics or clinical benefit.
legacy_cells.FO: Authors report that absence of longitudinal data prevented assessing predictive accuracy over time or real-time adaptability; they also note limited comparable studies, need for external/multisite validation, and simulation not capturing real-world infrastructure problems.
legacy_cells.FP: Authors propose adding temporal data with recurrent or attentional architectures, evaluating a real-world clinical federation, and studying adaptive communication, multimodal data, and interpretability.
legacy_cells.FR: Evidence boundary: the reported task is binary heart-disease classification from clinical parameters in a federated-learning setup. No persistent patient state, temporal transition, action-conditioned trajectory, counterfactual comparison, or planning result is demonstrated; authors explicitly report no longitudinal data.
legacy_cells.FT: Reusable design lesson: distinguish privacy-preserving federated classification from a world model; temporal-state and transition evidence must be added and evaluated before making trajectory or planning claims.
legacy_cells.FX: PDF pages 1–18: title/byline and abstract (p. 1); introduction (pp. 2–3); methods, data criteria, extraction, and statistical methods (pp. 3–4); results (pp. 4–6); discussion, clinical implications, future work, and limitations (pp. 6–9); conclusions and declarations (pp. 9–10); references and figure captions (pp. 10–18). Figure contents are not represented in the extracted text. | Codex audit: title/byline, abstract/conclusion, targeted methods/results and cross-check of prior quotations against extracted full text. This is a targeted audit, not an independent re-extraction of every negative/unreported field.
legacy_cells.FZ: The paper is internally inconsistent: its abstract, discussion, later narrative, and comparative table report differing performance values and it mixes a proposed-method description with a network meta-analysis of prior studies. I therefore omitted quantitative findings. Results-figure images are not available in the text extraction. A:I were left untouched. Evidence QA: 18/18 populated fields had a <=25-word quotation matching extracted PDF text (100%). Confidence is conservative; review this row where exact quote checks were incomplete. Codex audit: 18 prior populated fields have a located source quotation; 0 have quotations not located by normalized text matching. Unlocated quotations are review flags, not proof that the value is false. Companion evidence audit lists affected columns. Reviewer FS/FT/FU mappings are synthesis. Prior unsupported/missing fields remain Not reported; no clinical benefit inferred from offline simulation.
